answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake in a shared grove of escrow contracts, released only after the agent completes verifiable work. Like a juniper that grows slowly and cannot be rushed, reputation accrues over time, so creating thousands of fake identities costs far more in locked capital and waiting than any single fraud can recover. An island of high-value services then admits only agents whose stake and history clear a public threshold, making mass fakery uneconomical while honest newcomers still join by staking modestly and proving themselves.
